text: Hello, boys and girls.Good to see you again.In the previous lesson, we learned many things about electricity.In the story A Dangerous Servant, we learned facts about electricity, including what electricity is, where it comes from, and how it is stored.In Lessoning and Speaking lessons, we learned names of electrical appliances, and we talked about electrical safety at home and outside.In grammar lessons, we used modal verbs to tell people how to save electricity.Later, we used object clauses to express our opinions on some facts about electricity.Do you remember you wrote some sentences about what you wanted to know about some famous scientists and inventors?In our writing lesson, we wrote electrical safety rules for workplaces and schools.So, what do you think we are going to talk about in today's lesson?Today, we will read an article.This is the title.Electricity works everywhere.What does everywhere refer to?Will this article talk about the electricity we use at home or outside?Or will it talk about the electricity we use at workplace and at school?Or perhaps it is about electricity used in different countries?Open your textbooks and turn to page 46.Quickly go through the article, Electricity Works Everywhere, and answer the following questions.Time's up!Can you tell me what this article is mailing about?Yes, it's about uses of electricity.You've got it, right?Everywhere refers to every place in cities and in the countryside.How do you know that?Where did you find the answer?You find the answer in the last sentence, right?Let's take a close look at the passage.Can you find the topic sentence?Read the passage again and answer the question.What is the topic sentence in English?All right.Have you got the answers?What is the topic sentence?Usually, topic sentence is a sentence at the beginning of a paragraph.It states or suggests the main idea of the paragraph.The article we are reading only has one paragraph.Do you think the first sentence is the topic sentence?Yes, the first sentence in the passage.Almost everyone today uses electricity in one way or another.It's the topic sentence.Good.The sentence means today everyone uses electricity in many different ways.In other words, electricity is used everywhere.Does the writer use any detail to support the topic sentence?Of course.Then what details support the topic sentence?You've got them.The writer gives a lot of examples to support his idea.Many uses of electricity are mentioned in the passage.Electricity is used to?Pay attention to the phrases used here.The phrases should start with a verb.What is the first use the writer tells us in the passage?That's right.Light streets and buildings.Next,warm people and animals.Heat food in cookers and cool it in refrigerators.Drive trains and work traffic lights and lifts.Work machines in factories.Power computers,televisions and electrical machines.Anything else?Milk cows.Trop food and churn butter.Wait a second.What does churn butter mean?Churn is a verb.It means stir milk in a special container to make butter.Read after me.Churn.All the phrases start with a bare form of a verb.Because here,be used to is the passive form of use something to do something.What if we change the first part of the sentence into electricity is used for?Think about what kind of words or phrases you will put after for?Since for is a preposition,we should have nouns or noun phrases or gerund.So how should we change the phrases?Let's take a look.Electricity is used for?Lighting.Heating.Cooking.Cooling.Why do we cool food?Yes,to store the food for longer time.So we can use storage.Next,trains and traffic lights are part of?Transportation.Next one,manufacturing.Remember?We've learned the word in unit two.Next,we watch TV and play computer games for?Entertainment.Milking a cow is a type of?Farming.Next one,people use machines to chop the corn to harvest.Here's another example.Here,we can use agriculture.The last one,we use electrical machines to cool the milk and churn the butter.We call this process food production.The long verb phrases become much shorter and simpler nouns or noun phrases,right?We will use the phrases later in the class.Keep them in mind.We have talked about the first sentence and the details.Let's move on to the last sentence.Does the last sentence give a fitting conclusion?Why or why not?The last sentence.Indeed,electricity finds as much work to do in the country side as it does in the cities.Explains electricity plays an important role both in the country side and in the cities.It echoes the topic sentence.So the answer to the question will be yes.In the passage,the writer tells us many uses of electricity.We can pick what you think is the most important use of electricity.You know what?There's no correct answer to the question.You can pick what you think is the most important use in the text and explain your reasons.My student Tom would like to share his opinion.Listen.I think the most important use of electricity is powering the trains and traffic lights.Thanks to electricity,trains go much faster and faster.TheAnd people are able to get from one place to another more quickly.It's also clean energy.Traffic lights keep the traffic moving.We get to places more efficiently.Tom thinks transportation is the most important use.He stated his opinion and supported the opinion by facts or examples.Good job.But do you agree with him?Probably you have different ideas, right?The second question.What is the most surprising use of electricity?Mandy has her own opinion.I think the most surprising use of electricity is to run computers and televisions.These electrical devices entertain and inform people in our homes.But we hardly think about electricity when we watch TV or play computer games.Many of us take electricity for granted.Well, different people may have different opinions on the topic.What's your opinion?Share it with your friends via WeChat or QQ.One more question for you.Where is electricity needed and used more?In the cities or in the countryside?At the end of the passage, the writer tells uselectricity finds as much work to do in the countryside as it does in the cities.Do you agree with the writer?Julia has something to say.Julia, please.Electricity finds as much work to do in the countryside as it does in the cities.But because more things are happening in cities,and more people live in cities,I think electricity is needed and used more in the city.What do you think of Julia's idea?To answer this question, we can use some diagrams.Look at task 1 on your worksheet.There's a mind map in task 1.We have uses of electricity in the middle,and the city and the countryside branching out on either side.The passage describes how electricity is used in the cities and in the countryside.You can list the uses under each subhead and add others.Make connections between the two places.Have you finished your mind map?I will show you one of my students' mind map.Look at it.This student obviously found more uses of electricity in the cities than in the countryside.But there are some overlaps between them.一部分重叠的内容Have you noticed?Cooking appears in both sides.So do lighting and storage.I bet your mind map also has some overlaps.It seems it is not easy to classify uses of electricity by cities and countryside in this type of mind map.What might be a better way to categorize uses of electricity?Look at this diagram.We call it Venn diagram.Venn圖In its simplest form, it is two circles that overlap in the middle.The two circles refer to city and the countryside.The middle part is what they have in common.Now, use the Venn diagram to organize the uses.This is task two on your worksheet.We've learned a lot of uses of electricity from the passage.Feel free to use them in your Venn diagram.You can also add more uses if you think they are important.Have you finished?Compare the Venn diagram with the mind map you drew in task one.Which one is better?I think your Venn diagram may be pretty much like this sample.So, if you want to compare and contrast two things which have something in common,Venn diagram might be a better choice.Now, read the passage again and answer the following questions.What kind of text is it?Is it a story like a dangerous servant?Of course, it's different from a dangerous servant.Electricity Works Everywhere is an expository passage.This text lists and describes the uses of electricity in cities and the countryside.There is no plot or characters.Where would you find the text and what is its target audience?Electricity Works Everywhere might be found in an encyclopedia, on a website, in a newspaper, a magazine, or at an exhibition.The target audience is children, teenagers, adults who are interested in electricity and want to know more about it.The text language is simple and easy, and the passage provides facts and details of electricity.The main purpose is to inform.You get a lot of information from it, although it is such a short text.Have you ever noticed the verbs in the text?Do some of them sound strange to you?Kevin?I never know that milk can be used as a verb.Many words can be used in more than one part of speech.It is quite common that a word has two parts of speech.About one-fifth of all English verbs were originally nouns.Do you still remember the pictures?Cool can be used as both an adjective and a verb.Switch is used both as a noun and a verb.Technically, this very common process in English is known as conversion.It converts a word into a different part of speech.從理論上說,這是英語構詞法中常見的轉化法。轉化法將一個單詞轉化為不同的詞性。One particularly common form of conversion is using nouns as verbs, and sometimes adjectives as verbs.This specific process is called verbing.The purpose of verbing is to make what we say immediate and to the point.During situations in which a word is used repeatedly, verbing seems more common.To some, it is also a kind of word play.Verbing makes what you say sound fresher and less traditional.Can you find other examples of verbing in our text?Please read and underline them.Have you got them?Here they are.A question for you.Can chop and churn be used as nouns?If they can, what might they mean?Great!Both chop and churn can be used as nouns.We sometimes say a pork chop.It means a piece of pork with a bone still in it.And the word churn is a large container for making milk into butter.Now you know other examples of verbing in the text.Remember, if you can't find an existing verb to describe what you are doing, just use the nearest noun as a verb.Let's have some practice.Can you use these verbs to talk about electricity and its uses?The pictures are for your reference.This is task 3 on your worksheet.Take the first picture for instance.As a noun, toast means bread, which has been made brown and crisp by cooking at a high temperature.Toast can also be used as a verb.We can say, We can toast a pizza in an electric oven.Here it means, We heat the pizza in an electric oven.Okay, it's your turn now.Ready?The second picture.What cools the air in the room?Yes, the electric fan.Can we microwave an egg?Of course not.It is likely to explode.Electricity is sent to our flat through thin wires, isn't it?We can change wire into a verb.Before electricity is wired to our flat, it passes through a meter.Which costs less, electricity or petrol?Must be electricity, right?We can say, Electricity costs less than petrol, so powering an electric vehicle is cheaper.I believe the sentences on your worksheet must
